sections.designNote: Content-first split hero that answers what it is and who it is for immediately. Use the ad-matched headline, a short subheadline for IT teams, and a single solid orange Get started CTA. Right side should show a premium Endpoint Central console mockup with layered endpoint cards and a subtle human PNG for trust. Add a compact 3-bullet benefit strip below the CTA for continuity and clarity.

Immediate logo-first proof section beneath the hero. Use 3-6 recognizable enterprise/logos in a static flex-wrap grid. Since no customer logos are provided, use a metric-backed credibility strip only if actual logos cannot be sourced; otherwise keep it minimal and clean. Avoid marquee motion.

First product block should be the main conversion engine: 3-step how-it-works framing in a tabbed preview format so the buyer understands the workflow in under 60 seconds. Lead with the click-driving feature pair: Patch & Update Management and Vulnerability Remediation. The second product section should alternate to a split-panel list style, with the broader platform capabilities grouped into concise capability tiles. Keep copy short and operational, not marketing-heavy.

Optional and low emphasis. Since include=false, keep this section omitted or collapsed into a lightweight assurance strip only if needed for marketplace context. Do not let it compete with proof or product content.

Do not introduce a full pricing comparison because no pricing data is provided. If the page must support intent capture, use a narrow conversion nudge instead of a pricing module. Keep this out of the primary flow.

Use a credibility-heavy testimonial section with one featured quote and two supporting quotes, since there are 5 testimonials. Rotate around patching, remote support, and simplified deployment. Keep it visually calmer than the product blocks, with strong quote typography and author metadata.

Final conversion section should be a centered high-contrast card with minimal fields and one full-width mobile CTA. CTA text must remain Get started. Keep the form visually isolated and unmistakably final, with the orange button at 100% opacity and no secondary action.
Omit if no real press logos exist. If required, keep as a minimal credibility footer strip only, never animated, never dominant.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The hero headline is moderately long, so 48px keeps it strong without crowding the split layout.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen split or stacked hero with brand/logo placement, large centered headline, short supporting copy, and a compact benefit list below the fold of the hero text. Primary conversion action is placed prominently in the hero and repeated in the form area.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero first, then a high-intent lead form, followed by alternating content blocks that introduce the product value proposition and feature groupings. Rhythm favors short headline-led sections with concise supporting text and list-based detail rather than long prose.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Utility-first cards with light borders or subtle elevation, generous padding, clear heading hierarchy, and minimal decoration. Content is organized into rectangular modules that can hold feature titles, short descriptions, and optional icons.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA is singular and conversion-focused. Secondary CTAs are absent or de-emphasized. CTA placement follows a top-to-mid funnel pattern: hero, form header, and repeated within key sections if needed.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing module pattern is implied in this reference. If added, it should be isolated as a dedicated conversion section rather than embedded within feature content.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not represented in the provided reference fragment; assume a minimal utility footer if needed, with no heavy marketing content.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Low-media landing page pattern with logo usage in the hero and content driven primarily by text and lists. If media is introduced, it should be small, functional, and supportive rather than dominant.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Feature-group sections with one strong section headline and a grid of short feature tiles. Each tile contains a title and a concise benefit-oriented description. Grouping is by capability themes rather than by user journey.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead capture panel directly after the hero, using a titled card container and stacked fields. The form is visually separated from the hero and designed as an immediate conversion step with high emphasis.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, presentation-style layout with no explicit motion dependency. Any motion should be restrained and functional, such as subtle hover or entrance transitions only if needed.

designNotes: Favor straightforward B2B conversion hierarchy over visual storytelling.
Keep copy blocks compact and scannable.
Use a strong typographic hierarchy with large H1, medium section headers, and short body copy.
Prefer bordered cards and clean whitespace over heavy illustration.
Place trust-building elements near the top if available, but keep them lightweight and non-intrusive.

designStrategy.reasoning: This page is a single-product, demo-driven landing page for IT teams already solution-aware, so the best strategy is a product-led structure that converts quickly. The strongest trust signal is logos, so they should dominate the proof layer near the hero and not be buried. Because the content is medium-volume and feature-heavy, the layout should stay balanced: concise hero, immediate form, then tightly grouped capability sections with utility cards. A split hero is ideal here because it lets the page communicate the product value clearly while accommodating a human PNG for approachability and credibility. CTA intent should be strong and singular around Request Demo, with no competing secondary action. Testimonials should support conversion later in the page, ideally in a slider format to keep the page compact and dynamic.
